\begin{chapstatus}{Roadmap of this chapter}
By the end of the chapter you can:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item distinguish analog from digital information and count the values that n bits can represent
\item encode numbers, colours and text as bits: positional notation, hexadecimal, RGB565, ASCII
\item name the basic data structures and the properties of an algorithm
\end{enumerate}
It builds on: only the setup of Chapter~\ref{ch:setup}. Next: Chapter~\ref{ch:integers}.
\par\smallskip\textbf{Looking back, looking ahead.} In Lecture 02 the instruction addi t1, t1, 1 appeared in memory as the word 0x00130313. Today the same 32 bits can be read as a number, a colour, four letters or an instruction: the code decides. Lecture 19 reads the instruction field by field. \emph{Recall:} Name two different things one 32-bit word can mean, and what decides which meaning applies.
\end{chapstatus}
